segments.text: I learned much later that something had begun growing in the wreckage of a battle.
From a severed piece of the Reptilian Emperor himself, at the time.
None of us knew I was a boy, and my world was still small.
I used to spend my afternoons drawing the old bridge near our village.
I drew it so often that I thought I knew every stone I suppose children believe
that the things they know will always be there.
My mother was a healer. People came to her with broken bones, fevers, and troubles that
had nothing to do with the medicine. I remember thinking that she could mend almost anything.
The first signs of war came from beyond the hills, smoke. Then strange lights in the sky.
The adults knew more than they told us.
I remember how carefully they began choosing their words.
We left before dawn, I carried my sketchbook.
Because I couldn't think of anything else worth taking.
I looked back at the bridge until the road turned.
And I couldn't see it anymore.
I thought we'd return in a few days.
We reached Ashbridge with hundreds of other refugees.
My mother began helping in the infirmary almost immediately.
That was where I first saw Kesh,
A reptilian boy whose injuries had brought him far from his own world.
Keshe had a soldier's confidence, although he was no older than I was.
He thought my drawings were inaccurate.
I thought he was insufferably certain of himself.
Somehow.
Now, that was enough to begin a friendship.
Roque arrived with refugees from Morvay.
He was a young werewolf.
And at first I was frightened of him.
I had heard too many stories about the creatures of his world.
Most of those stories had been told by people
Who had never met one.
One afternoon, we spent hours trying to repair a broken card.
Keshe understood the mechanism.
I had drawn a solution, and Rook could see what neither of us had noticed.
It was the first time we accomplished something together.
We were three boys from three worlds, with different bodies, different childhoods, and
different ideas about almost everything I didn't understand.
Why we felt so familiar to one another.
Ashbridge was full of people who had nowhere else to go.
My mother worked in the infirmary.
Some of the patients came from our world.
Others came from places we hadn't even known existed.
We found it in a room where they kept things brought through the crossings.
It was small, dark, and covered in tiny moving threads.
Someone had sealed it inside a glass chamber.
Nobody seemed to know what it was.
At first, we thought it simply moved toward our hands.
Then I drew a little mark on the glass.
It copied me.
When we returned the next day, it remembered.
That was when I began to think it was trying to speak to us.
My mother warned us not to open the chamber.
The organism wasn't from our world, and nobody knew what it might do.
Then the fighting reached Ashbridge.
We were ordered to leave, and there wasn't enough time to take everything.
I remember Keshe watching the doorway, I remember Rook breaking the glass, and I remember the
creature crawling into my hands, at the time, I thought we'd save the life, I remember the
sound of that glass more clearly than almost anything else.
The war followed us, wherever we went, soldiers fought over roads, bridges, and the passages
between worlds.
We tried to stay ahead of them, and beneath my coat, I carried something nobody knew about.
We needed a name for it I chose, Thred, because the little strands that moved across its body.
Keshe thought I could have been more imagined, but whenever I called it by that name, it
came toward me. Near the machine factories, thread would sit for hours watching the mechanisms
move. Everything there seemed perfectly organized. Soon it began arranging stones, scraps in
piece arranging stones, and pieces of wire into patterns of its own. It became distressed
...whenever we disturbed.
